controlFrameAccessSpecification.targetConstraint: An independently adjudicated malicious-publication or maintainer-compromise manifest must cover a declared observation horizon; advisory absence remains unknown.

relatednessProtocol.relatedFamilyBoundary: The Mini Shai-Hulud atool and Keyv/Cacheable families must remain in one documented related-family validation cluster if a future manifest is eligible for a benchmark join.

purposeAndScope.purpose: Pre-register how a future target-matched outcome manifest must be independently adjudicated, coverage-audited, checksum-sealed, and withheld from feature collection until quality control is complete.
purposeAndScope.unit: One canonical npm package-version candidate with a documented event-time decision and a separate coverage decision for its declared outcome horizon.
purposeAndScope.noCurrentOutcomeBoundary: This protocol does not contact incident sources, registries, advisory feeds, provider datasets, package artifacts, repositories, or any outcome endpoint. It does not add, alter, confirm, reject, or re-time any existing incident ledger record.
purposeAndScope.noControlBoundary: A non-event outcome can exist only after source-specific completeness for the entire row horizon and registered exclusions are proven. Source omission, advisory absence, registry survival, no-known-event language, or lack of a matching record remains unknown.
purposeAndScope.noModelBoundary: The protocol does not create a population, outcome row, target label, control, feature join, split, score, rank, interval, calibration result, model, or predictive metric.

allRequiredBeforeOutcomeSourceContact: The declared target is limited to independently adjudicated future malicious publication or maintainer compromise; ordinary vulnerability status is not a substitute target.
A field-complete source-inventory plan, outcome-horizon plan, adjudication handbook, conflict-of-interest policy, and public-safe release policy are versioned and checksum-sealed.
Reviewers and source collectors cannot access feature values, feature quality-control outputs, review-queue membership, model scores, ranks, controls, or split assignments.
An access-controlled evidence docket store and immutable decision ledger are provisioned outside the public repository with key custody and retention policies documented.
The prospective population owner agrees to receive no outcome manifest until the feature and raw-evidence quality-control seals required by the separate contracts are complete.
prohibitedActivationFallbacks: Do not repurpose an advisory or vulnerability feed as closed-world malicious-publication or maintainer-compromise coverage.
Do not treat a current source page, later repository remediation, deletion, package unavailability, or current account status as an event-time observation.
Do not open an outcome source merely to enrich, repair, balance, or evaluate a feature table, control list, ranking, or model result.

targetVocabulary.future_confirmed_compromise: A technically corroborated targeted maintainer, publisher, account, or release-path compromise with exact npm affected-version evidence and adjudicated event start within the pre-registered horizon.
targetVocabulary.future_malicious_publication: A technically corroborated malicious npm package publication with exact affected-version evidence and adjudicated event start within the pre-registered horizon, excluding ordinary vulnerabilities.
targetVocabulary.unknown_outcome: Coverage, timing, version identity, target fit, or horizon completeness is absent or ambiguous. This is not benign, unaffected, safe, or a control.
targetVocabulary.excluded_not_target_matched: Evidence concerns an ordinary vulnerability, a non-npm system, no exact package-version identity, or another pre-registered exclusion; it is not a negative outcome.

horizonRules: Declare and checksum-seal the interval (feature_cutoff_at_utc, horizon_end_at_utc] before a source inventory is opened.
A positive event start must lie inside the declared interval; later discovery does not move its event start backward without independently documented time evidence.
A row with incomplete source coverage or an unobservable full horizon remains unknown or is right-censored under the frozen rule, never a control.

Source collection after horizon end may document historical coverage only when the source’s release/retrieval chronology and completeness scope are explicitly recorded; it may not create retrospective feature evidence.

sourceInventoryAndProvenanceSchema.description: One pre-registered source inventory record per future source before candidate-docket review. This artifact contains field names only, not sources or observed values.
sourceAcceptanceRules: A source must document its scope, time coverage, target semantics, version identity handling, and access provenance sufficiently to support a field-specific decision.
Primary or authoritative incident evidence and independent technical corroboration are captured as separate source objects where the target definition requires corroboration.
An OpenSSF, OSV, GitHub Advisory, provider, registry, or scanner record may support candidate discovery or corroboration only under its documented scope; absence never supplies a negative label.
Source inventories must preserve coverage limitations and retractions as first-class records rather than silently replacing or deleting prior source versions.

reviewSeparation: Assign each docket to at least two independent adjudicators who cannot access feature values, candidate priority, control status, outcome prevalence, model results, or split assignments.
Each adjudicator records a decision and reason codes before seeing the other adjudicator’s decision.
A third adjudicator or pre-registered panel resolves disagreement; preserve the initial decisions, reconciliation rationale, timestamps, and conflicts in the immutable ledger.

An adjudicated positive requires exact npm package-version identity, event-time support, target match, and the frozen corroboration threshold. Otherwise record unknown or excluded_not_target_matched rather than negative.
conflictAndRetractionRules: Record reviewer conflicts, source conflicts, retractions, supersessions, and unresolved ambiguity without overwriting prior decisions.
A sealed manifest revision may be superseded only by a new immutable revision with a parent-manifest hash, change log, and pre-registered policy basis; do not mutate the prior manifest in place.
Do not derive event timing from a remediation commit, source retrieval time, or current package state when evidence for event start is absent.

allowedDecisions.positive_in_horizon: Exact adjudicated package-version event matches the target and has an event start inside the frozen horizon.
allowedDecisions.eligible_non_event_after_complete_covera: Only permitted after source-specific completeness for the entire horizon, all registered exclusions, and independent quality control; it remains unavailable until the control-frame gate opens.
allowedDecisions.unknown_or_coverage_incomplete: Coverage, target fit, event time, package-version identity, or the full horizon is absent or ambiguous.
allowedDecisions.excluded_or_right_censored: A frozen exclusion or right-censoring rule applies; this is not a non-event/control label.

prohibitedShortcuts: Do not infer a non-event from missing source membership, advisory absence, registry persistence, package deletion, lack of a malware report, or no-known-event language.
Do not classify an entire package as a positive or non-event when the target is version-specific and the evidence does not identify an exact affected version.
Do not downgrade an ambiguous positive candidate into a non-event/control merely to complete a matched set or balance classes.

secureOnlyFields: Exact package names and versions before source terms and the public-release policy permit disclosure.
Raw source objects, evidence text, reviewer identities, sensitive source references, adjudication notes, conflict disclosures, keyed mappings, and any feature or population identifiers.

Target outcomes, controls, join results, family or validation assignments, model artifacts, ranks, metrics, and row-level coverage decisions before the quality-control seal and applicable release authorization.
orderedWorkflow: Checksum-seal the source inventory, target/horizon contract, adjudication handbook, relatedness rules, and public-release policy before source collection.
Collect source objects and candidate dockets in an access-controlled evidence store while outcomes remain inaccessible to feature collectors and population owners.
Complete independent adjudication, coverage review, retraction review, and source-quality control without feature, score, or split access.
Compute and record Merkle roots and a manifest byte checksum; seal the manifest with immutable parent revision linkage.
Release only the public-safe sealing manifest and permitted aggregates until source terms and quality policy permit row-level release.
Permit a separate authorized join only after the population, feature, raw-evidence, and outcome quality-control seals all pass; record the join as a new artifact rather than mutating this manifest.
blindingRules: Outcome adjudicators must not receive feature values, authority commitments, graph measures, workflow evidence, review-queue membership, controls, scores, ranks, or performance metrics.

Feature and raw-evidence collectors must not receive candidate dockets, source evidence, outcome decisions, coverage decisions, family assignments, or target prevalence until their own quality-control seals are final.
No party may use preliminary positive counts, class balance, or missingness to modify source inclusion, adjudication, outcome horizon, feature definition, or population query.

relatednessAndJoinBoundary.requirement: After outcome adjudication but before any eligible split, map documented incident-family and cross-family relatedness to the frozen validation-unit registry. Preserve an explicit unknown-relatedness state rather than assuming independence.
relatednessAndJoinBoundary.inheritedValidationUnitRule: Use the grouped-inference protocol’s connected-component validation units; do not split Mini Shai-Hulud atool and Keyv/Cacheable across partitions because documented payload lineage prevents an independence claim.
prohibitedInterpretations: An incident family is not automatically an attacker identity, causal chain, or independent observation.
A sealed outcome manifest is not a fitted dataset, temporal split, resample, control frame, or model evaluation.
This protocol is not an outcome manifest, an incident-source audit, a positive-label expansion, a control frame, or a benchmark result.

A source inventory, docket identifier, digest, Merkle root, opaque reference, or sealing manifest is integrity metadata only; it does not establish that a package version is positive, unaffected, safe, benign, or trusted.
No non-event/control, score, rank, model, interval, calibration, or predictive metric may be inferred or computed from this protocol.
Existing strict incident records remain independently adjudicated positive evidence only; they are not a closed-world outcome population or proof of horizon completeness.
